readings.title: The exchange with two teachers
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Sunrise Skills Exchange paired an older gardener with a young volunteer who understood video editing. Organisers initially described the project as young people teaching older residents technology. During their first meeting, however, the gardener explained planting methods that the volunteer wanted to record. Each became teacher and learner at different moments. The project changed its publicity to reflect the exchange. Age alone had not predicted who held useful knowledge. The pair worked best when they began by asking what each person could offer and what each hoped to learn.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: The pace of a shared lesson
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: In a mixed-age music group, one learner read notation quickly while another remembered melodies by ear. The tutor first interpreted different speeds as differences in effort. After asking learners to explain their approach, she realised that the task favoured one kind of experience. She combined a printed example with a recording and time to practise. Neither method suited everyone equally, but more learners could begin successfully. The lesson did not prove that people of a certain age always learnt in a particular way. It showed the value of asking individuals rather than assigning them to a simple category.

readings.title: A story recorded together
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A teenager helped her grandfather record a description of his first railway journey. She wanted to shorten long pauses, while he felt some pauses expressed the difficulty of remembering. They listened together and agreed which sections to edit. She learnt that technical neatness was not the only aim, and he learnt how editing could make a recording easier to follow. The final version carried a note saying it had been edited with the speaker's agreement. Working together required discussion about purpose as well as skill with a device. Neither person's preference automatically settled every choice.

readings.title: The invitation that changed
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A centre advertised an activity as 'Lessons for the elderly from young experts'. Several older residents felt the wording assumed they lacked useful abilities, while young volunteers worried that 'experts' overstated their knowledge. The centre renamed it 'Bring a Skill, Learn a Skill' and asked all participants to list interests. Attendance improved, though organisers still needed to provide suitable seating and clear schedules. A new title did not solve every access problem. It removed one unnecessary assumption and made the invitation more consistent with the equal exchange the centre hoped to create.

translation.stem:
Translate the following original passage into Chinese. Preserve the meaning and logical relationships.

People of different ages often possess different kinds of knowledge. An exchange works well when neither side is treated as having nothing to offer. Patience and mutual respect allow both people to ask questions. The strongest learning relationships are built on curiosity rather than assumptions.
translation.referenceAnswer: 不同年龄的人往往拥有不同类型的知识。只有双方都不被视为没有东西可教给对方时，交流才会顺利。耐心和相互尊重让双方都能提问。最牢固的学习关系建立在好奇心之上，而不是建立在先入为主的判断之上。
translation.explanation: 参考译文仅示范一种表达。评分时关注信息完整性、转折和条件等逻辑关系；意思准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write an English response of about 120 words to the following original simulation task. Use your own examples and organise your ideas clearly.

Discuss the benefits of people of different ages learning together. Describe an activity and explain how to avoid treating either group as less capable.
writing.sampleAnswer: Learning across generations can reveal skills that age-based assumptions hide. For example, an older gardener and a younger video editor could make a short planting guide together. One would explain gardening decisions, while the other would demonstrate recording and editing. Both would have opportunities to ask questions and teach. Organisers should invite participants to describe their interests instead of assigning the older person the role of learner automatically. Sessions should allow enough time for discussion and provide equipment everyone can use comfortably. When preferences differ, the pair should return to the purpose of the project. Mutual respect grows when each person has meaningful control over the shared work and can see the value of the other's contribution.
writing.explanation: 范文供完成作答后对照。允许不同立场与例子；围绕题目要求论述清楚、理由充分、语言准确即可。
